newsitem.title: USA: Xerox cancels $2.7 billion sale of Talegen to KKR.
newsitem.headline: Xerox cancels $2.7 billion sale of Talegen to KKR.

text.p: Xerox Corp. said Wednesday it cancelled the $2.7 billion sale of its Talegen Holdings Inc. property and casualty insurance business to investor groups led by Wall Street buyout firm Kohlberg Kravis Roberts & Co.

The companies said they "have mutually agreed to terminate the transactions for Xerox to sell the remaining Talegen Holdings, Inc., property and casualty insurance units and The Resolution Group (TRG) to investor groups led by KKR."

Stamford, Conn.-based Xerox, the nation's biggest copier maker, wants to sell the Talegen property and casualty insurance units as soon as possible, as it tries to exit the financial services business.
"Both parties worked hard and diligently to complete the transactions as originally envisioned," Xerox Chairman Paul Allaire said in a statement.

"When it became clear that this could not be accomplished consistent with all the prevailing considerations of both parties, Xerox and KKR decided it was best to terminate the transactions," Allaire said.

KKR representatives declined to elaborate on why the deal was cancelled or to comment on whether they would seek any other deals in the insurance business. Xerox representatives were not immediately available for comment.

In connection with the anticipated sale, last year Xerox took a $1.5 billion charge against earnings to reflect a $975 million loss on the sale and $525 million to strengthen Talegen's cushion for losses against future claims.
Xerox said no additional charges were required as a result of Wednesday's announcement.
The sale, announced Jan. 18, would have ended Xerox's failed attempt to diversify into financial services.
The troubles with Talegen, which was a drag on earnings and had depressed Xerox's stock price, were not what managers had envisioned when Xerox bought the business in the early 1980s.
Xerox, like many companies at the time, was diversifying to find new sources of earnings to help it offset swings in the economy and stiff competition from Japanese copier makers.
